title: Bollywood's Last Gentlemen: How Ajay Devgn and Akshay Kumar Quietly Avoided a ₹200 Crore Clash
excerpt: In an industry where ego routinely trumps box office sense, two veterans just showed everyone how it's done.
body:
In Bollywood, box office clashes are blood sport. Studios weaponize release dates. Stars trade barbs through "sources close to the production." Marketing teams go to war. So when two of Hindi cinema's biggest names quietly picked up the phone and agreed to move out of each other's way, it was — by industry standards — practically revolutionary.

The Near-Miss

Here's what almost happened: Ajay Devgn's 'Dhamaal 4' was set for July 3, 2026. Akshay Kumar's 'Welcome to the Jungle' — the third instalment of the beloved comedy franchise directed by Anees Bazmee — had locked June 26. That's a seven-day gap between two massive comedy tentpoles targeting the exact same audience during peak summer season.

Seven days isn't enough. Both films would have cannibalised each other's second-weekend numbers, splitting the comedy-going audience and leaving both franchises limping toward underwhelming lifetime totals.

The Phone Call

According to Bollywood Hungama, the resolution came through direct conversation between the two camps. Ajay Devgn agreed to shift 'Dhamaal 4' to July 17, giving 'Welcome to the Jungle' a clean three-week theatrical window before the next comedy juggernaut arrived. Trade analyst Taran Adarsh confirmed the move on X, calling it a "gentleman's agreement."

The term matters. In an industry where Rajamouli and Nag Ashwin don't blink at clashing with Bollywood, and where Shah Rukh Khan once went head-to-head with Aamir Khan during Christmas, a voluntary date-shift signals something increasingly rare: professional maturity.

Why It's Good Business

The math is simple. India's multiplex infrastructure has grown, but comedy audiences still overlap heavily. Both franchises — 'Dhamaal' with its slapstick ensemble energy and 'Welcome' with its NRI-flavoured absurdity — target the 18–45 urban audience that buys weekend tickets. A clash would have forced both films into aggressive pricing wars and expanded show-count battles, with neither achieving its full potential.

By spacing the releases three weeks apart, both films now have room to breathe. 'Welcome to the Jungle' gets June 26 to mid-July essentially to itself. 'Dhamaal 4' gets the July 17 slot with reduced competition and the benefit of any residual comedy appetite in the market.

Summer 2026: Comedy Season

The broader picture is that Bollywood is betting heavily on comedy this summer. After the action-thriller fatigue of early 2026 — where multiple dark, intense films underperformed — studios are pivoting back to the genre that has always been Hindi cinema's most reliable money-maker.

'Welcome to the Jungle' brings back the franchise's signature blend of mistaken identities, underworld parodies, and the kind of family-friendly chaos that works across demographics. 'Dhamaal 4' doubles down on its own established formula: ensemble comedy with increasingly outlandish set pieces.

The Diaspora Connection

For NRIs, both films represent the kind of "go with the whole family" cinema that Indian diaspora communities love. Weekend screenings of Bollywood comedies at Regal Cinemas in Edison, Cineplex in Brampton, or Cineworld in Leicester are social events — and having them spaced out means families don't have to choose. June 26 for 'Welcome,' July 17 for 'Dhamaal' — that's two guaranteed family outings instead of a forced pick-one scenario.

In a summer already packed with Hollywood tentpoles, Bollywood's comedy duo just made sure the desi audience doesn't have to split their loyalties. That's not just smart scheduling — it's respect for the audience.
